_about: ENGLISH COPY OVERRIDES for steps whose source JSON is generated.
src/data/steps.feature.json and steps.short.json are rewritten by
`npm run extract`, which parses legacy/. A sentence corrected there is
correct until the next extraction and then silently is not — so this
file carries the corrections instead, and extract cannot reach it.
It is the same shape of answer as steps.tanglish.json, which holds the
full Tanglish translations for the same reason, and steps.priority.json,
which holds the spine. src/ui/steps.js merges all three. The cost is the
one steps.priority.json already names in its own notes: a fact about a
step now lives in two files, split by whether the file happens to be
generated, and the two halves can drift. That cost is accepted
deliberately here, because the alternative is worse — teaching the
extractor to rewrite prose would end the property that makes
`npm run extract` deterministic and byte-identical against legacy/.
KEYED `<ns>:<stepId>`, the same key steps.tanglish.json uses, so one
mental model covers both. `deck` replaces the step's deck; `why` is
keyed by the INDEX of the why block within that step, counted the way
renderStep() counts it.
The override is applied BEFORE render, not after, so the corrected
English is what the EN map stores — which means toggling to Tanglish
and back returns to the correction rather than to the sentence it
replaced. An override applied to the DOM afterwards would be undone by
the first language toggle.
Keep this small. It is for copy that has gone WRONG, not for copy
somebody wants to reword — rewording belongs in legacy/ and the
extractor, where it stays one source.

why.0: For each beat, write 1–3 sentences. Not the scene — the function. Dragon's fifteen are laid out below the table as a compass.
